youtube.title: WEEKLY ROUNDUP
youtube.summary: Dieuwe de Boer and William McGimpsey return for a Weekly Roundup covering unrest in France, Brian Tamaki’s prosecution for alleged incitement of racial disharmony and New Zealand’s election debates. They examine free speech concerns, the coalition government’s record on crime and education, and the risks of strategic voting. They also explore Winston Peters’ immigration policies and whether political pressure could shift public opinion towards remigration. youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan’s weekly interview with Winston Peters focuses on New Zealand First’s push to protect cash, concerns over proposed online safety laws and restrictions on under-16s, and the MMP overhang debate. Peters also criticises the political establishment’s handling of COVID-19, condemns political engagement with gangs, and argues for controlled immigration and stronger accountability. youtube.title: FIONA ANDERSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Fiona Anderson, manager of Piha Campground, after Auckland Council’s local board unanimously approved its reopening for the summer. Fiona credits the community’s resilience and successful challenge to a one-size-fits-all approach to flood risk. She discusses the campground’s future, ongoing council accountability and the need for elected representatives to put local communities first. To find out more visit Piha Campground For Community news that gets results, sign up for RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: ANDREW LOWENTHAL
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with Andrew Lowenthal, journalist and founder of Liber-net, about Australia’s proposed Digital Duty of Care Bill and its implications for free speech and privacy. They examine vague definitions of online harm, potential government surveillance through AI-powered “sock puppet” identities, and the under-16 social media ban. Lowenthal argues the measures risk censorship, undermine parental responsibility and expand government control over online expression. Discover more from Andrew at Brownstone or find him on X Find from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: PATRICK WOOD
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Patrick Wood, independent journalist and founder of Technocracy News, about his new book Crucible of Tokens and the implications of asset tokenisation. Patrick argues that converting homes, shares and other assets into digital tokens could separate people from legal ownership, leaving them dependent on custodians for access. For more information: Check out Technocracy News or find Patrick on Substack His Substack article | Beware of tokenized gold as industry For an excerpt of Crucible of Tokens For more on Patrick's books

youtube.title: DAVID HARVEY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with former District Court judge David Harvey about Labour’s proposed ban on social media for under-16s and a digital duty of care for online platforms. Harvey argues that vague safety requirements could lead to state-backed censorship, expanded broadcasting regulation and restrictions on freedom of expression, while undermining parental rights. youtube.title: GARRICK CARR & MARK CROOKSTON
youtube.summary: Simon O’Connor speaks with Mark Crookston, Director of Digital at the National Library and Archives New Zealand, and Garrick Parr, Pacific Area Manager of FamilySearch International, about their partnership making historical records easier to discover. They explain how Papers Past’s millions of digitised pages can help people uncover family stories, strengthen their sense of identity and explore New Zealand’s past, with full-text searches making discoveries far easier than searching old microfilm. For more information: National Library | Papers Past Family Search
